/reaction-test.title: Visual Reaction Time Test
/reaction-test.subtitle: Benchmark visual response latency with high-resolution timing

sections.heading: What is Reaction Time?
paragraphs: Reaction time measures the duration between the presentation of a sensory stimulus and the initiation of an appropriate motor response.

In simple visual reaction time tasks, an individual responds to a single visual trigger using a single predefined input action, reflecting visual sensory transmission, central processing, and motor output initiation.

sections.heading: How the PULSE Test Works
paragraphs: The PULSE visual reaction assessment consists of 10 trials designed to measure rapid visual detection.

Each trial displays a waiting state followed by a randomized foreperiod delay between 100ms and 3000ms. When the interface transitions to the active stimulus, respond immediately using the spacebar or screen tap.
listItems: Randomized foreperiods split between short and long intervals to prevent anticipation
False starts recorded if input occurs before the stimulus appears or within 80ms

sections.heading: How Results Are Measured
paragraphs: Latency is captured using browser performance timestamps recorded at stimulus onset and input event dispatch.

To account for display refresh intervals, PULSE applies an estimated display refresh adjustment modeled at half the estimated frame interval. This correction represents a mathematical model of display presentation rather than physical hardware sensor telemetry.

sections.heading: Factors That Influence Scores
paragraphs: Reaction time fluctuates based on physiological and environmental factors, including sleep quality, circadian rhythms, caffeine intake, mental fatigue, and environmental distractions.

sections.heading: Hardware and Environmental Latency
paragraphs: Browser-based benchmarks are subject to external latency factors outside software control. Input-device polling intervals, display refresh rates, browser rendering pipelines, wireless connections, and operating system event scheduling all introduce variance.
While PULSE accounts for display frame intervals, local hardware transmission delays cannot be eliminated.

sections.heading: Consistent Testing Practices
paragraphs: For reliable longitudinal comparison, benchmark under consistent conditions: use wired input peripherals where available, test at similar times of day, and minimize background computer processing.

sections.heading: Interpreting Your Score
paragraphs: Session summaries report median latency, mean latency, and consistency scores across valid trials. Fast anticipatory attempts under 80ms are flagged as false starts to maintain benchmark validity.

sections.heading: Testing Scope and Limitations
paragraphs: PULSE provides browser-based performance benchmarking for personal tracking and research telemetry. It is not an instrument for medical, neurological, or attention deficit evaluation.

faq.question: Why do reaction times differ across devices?
faq.answer: Operating systems, display panels, and input controllers each introduce variable latency, producing slight differences between phones, tablets, and desktop computers.

faq.question: Can visual reaction time improve with practice?
faq.answer: Consistent testing can improve familiarity, motor readiness, and response consistency, though physiological limits constrain absolute reaction thresholds.

faq.question: What counts as a false start?
faq.answer: Inputs initiated while the stimulus is waiting or within 80ms of stimulus presentation are recorded as false starts.

/direction-test.title: Directional Choice Reaction Test
/direction-test.subtitle: Measure visual discrimination and choice response speed

sections.heading: What is Choice Reaction Time?
paragraphs: Choice reaction time requires identifying a specific stimulus and selecting the matching response action among multiple options.
Unlike simple reaction tests with a single trigger, choice tasks engage sensory identification, cognitive spatial mapping, and motor selection.

sections.heading: How the Test Works
paragraphs: The directional test presents 10 trials featuring arrow stimuli facing Up, Down, Left, or Right.
Respond as quickly and accurately as possible using corresponding arrow keys or on-screen directional buttons.
listItems: Four cardinal directions randomized per trial

sections.heading: Speed and Accuracy Balance
paragraphs: Performance is evaluated across both mean response time on correct choices and overall directional accuracy percentage.

sections.heading: Scope and Testing Factors
paragraphs: Physical keyboard layout, key switch travel, and touch responsiveness affect latency. This assessment serves as an educational benchmark and is not a clinical diagnostic measure.

faq.question: Why is choice reaction time slower than simple reaction time?
faq.answer: Choice tasks require sensory discrimination and action selection stages before motor command initiation, adding cognitive processing time.

/colour-recognition.title: Colour Recognition & Interference Test
/colour-recognition.subtitle: Evaluate selective attention with an interactive Stroop-style conflict task

sections.heading: Cognitive Conflict and Interference
paragraphs: This task measures selective attention and cognitive control when processing competing information streams.
In Stroop-style conflict paradigms, automated reading processes can interfere with naming font ink colors when word meaning and ink color diverge.

sections.heading: Assessment Structure
paragraphs: The test consists of 15 rounds alternating between congruent and incongruent trials.
A prompt indicates whether to match the text meaning or the font color using five shuffled color choice buttons.
listItems: Dynamic matching rules (Word meaning vs Font color)
Shuffled response options to prevent static spatial memorization

sections.heading: Interference Cost and Accuracy
paragraphs: Scores summarize overall response latency, accuracy rates, and the interference cost representing latency differences between conflicting and congruent rounds.

sections.heading: Display Considerations and Scope
paragraphs: Screen color calibration, ambient lighting, and display contrast influence color perception. This task is an educational cognitive benchmark, not a clinical test for color vision deficiency.

faq.question: Why do button positions shuffle?
faq.answer: Shuffling button positions ensures each response requires active visual identification rather than habitual spatial motor memory.

/block-memory.title: Block Memory Test
/block-memory.subtitle: Assess spatial sequence memory through progressive 9-block tapping patterns

sections.heading: Spatial Working Memory
paragraphs: Spatial working memory supports the temporary retention and sequential recall of visual locations in space.
It plays a fundamental role in navigation, spatial reasoning, and visual-motor coordination.

sections.heading: Sequence Recall Mechanics
paragraphs: A 3x3 grid of 9 blocks highlights in a random sequence. Once playback concludes, tap the blocks in the identical order.
The sequence starts at length 2 and increases by one block with each successful round. Users start with 3 lives.
listItems: Sequence progression starting at level 1 with 2 blocks

sections.heading: Progression and Span Score
paragraphs: Your final benchmark reflects the highest sequence span correctly completed before all 3 lives are exhausted.

sections.heading: Scope and Strategies
paragraphs: Visual path chunking and pattern association can aid recall. This benchmark is provided for personal tracking and cognitive exploration, not neurological memory diagnosis.

faq.question: How quickly do blocks flash?
faq.answer: Each block highlights for 400ms followed by a 200ms inter-stimulus pause before moving to the next position in the sequence.

/number-memory.title: Number Memory Test
/number-memory.subtitle: Benchmark short-term digit recall capacity across increasing numerical sequences

sections.heading: Digit Span Working Memory
paragraphs: Forward digit span measures the capacity of verbal working memory to temporarily retain and reproduce an arbitrary sequence of numbers.
It reflects storage capacity in short-term memory systems without long-term encoding.

sections.heading: How the Assessment Operates
paragraphs: Sequences begin at level 1 with 3 digits and increase by one digit with each successful round.
Numbers appear on screen for a duration scaled to the digit count before clearing. Enter the sequence using the number pad or keyboard. You have 3 lives.
listItems: Exposure time scaled to sequence length

sections.heading: Scoring and Level Advancement
paragraphs: Correct entries advance you to longer sequences, while incorrect submissions deplete lives. Your recorded score is the highest level achieved.

sections.heading: Strategies and Scope
paragraphs: Chunking numbers into rhythmically grouped subsets can aid recall. This test is an educational benchmark, not a standardized psychometric IQ assessment.

faq.question: How long is each number displayed?
faq.answer: Exposure time scales dynamically with digit length, providing sufficient time to read each numerical string before input begins.
